key_themes: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately amid personal scandal (alleged affair with Chinese spy), triggering broad AI/neocloud selloff
AI infrastructure earnings surge: Cisco and Applied Materials both post record quarterly revenues driven by AI demand
Rising Treasury yields hit 5.10%, fueling inflation fears and broad market pressure

stocks.reason: CEO Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately amid personal scandal including alleged affair with a reported Chinese spy; Colette Kress (CFO) named Interim CEO; multiple analyst downgrades (Bernstein, Oppenheimer, Evercore ISI)

Fell 6.37% on Thursday as NVIDIA CEO resignation spooked AI infrastructure investors; CoreWeave is heavily reliant on NVDA GPUs; stock had surged 25% Wednesday on its own strong Q3 earnings beat-and-raise
Reported record fiscal Q1 FY2027 revenue of $18.5B (+24% YoY), beat adjusted EPS estimate ($1.40 vs $1.32), raised full-year revenue guidance to $74.8B-$75.8B; shares rose ~3% after hours
Record fiscal Q4 FY2026 revenue of $10.41B (+53% YoY), beat estimates; guided Q1 FY2027 to $11.1B vs $10.84B consensus; AI chip demand driving growth
Upgraded by William Blair to Outperform from Market Perform; shares gained ~4% as investors rotated from NVIDIA to AMD following NVDA CEO resignation news
Shares rose 7.40% after news that co-founder Brian Halligan is returning to a leadership role, seen as a positive catalyst for strategy and growth
Dropped 16-17% after lowering 2026 revenue outlook to the low end of its $3.0B-$3.4B range due to revenue shifting to 2027; major disappointing guidance cut
Jumped nearly 10% after reporting adjusted quarterly EPS of $0.49, above the $0.47 consensus estimate; strong execution highlighted
Fell more than 9% after quarterly revenue of $1.59B missed consensus of approximately $1.77B; one of the largest single-day decliners on earnings
Upgraded by DZ Bank from Hold to Buy; also named as among the top market cap movers on Thursday alongside NVDA
Downgraded by Stifel from Buy to Hold (target cut to $2.50) after LS Power made a non-binding $2.00/share acquisition offer; stock faces uncertainty around deal viability
Downgraded by Bernstein to Market Perform from Outperform, with price target trimmed to $122; part of broad energy sector reassessment
Downgraded by Piper Sandler to Neutral from Overweight, citing dividend risk and pressure on consumer staples amid higher rates
Upgraded by Barclays to Equal Weight from Underweight with new $23 price target; improved near-term steel market outlook
